text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: p95 increase detected on runtime service after release 2026-03-wave-7. Canary traffic showing latency jump and kernel fallback noise. Alert ID: ALERT-RT-8321.

jamie: seeing p50 ~90ms -> 350ms, p95 ~220ms -> 1.1s, errors up ~0.8%. repro on eu-region canary nodes.

leo: confirmed. logs show repeated kernel-selector fallback to generic path + batching window shrink. error logs: 
```
WARN kernel_selector: fallback to generic_kernel v2 due to kernel_compile_timeout
ERROR batch_manager: microbatch window collapsed: target=16 got=2
```

sarah: was the thin-slice rollout included in this wave? I see feature-flag wave-7 enabled thin-slice-kernel.

jamie: yes, release manifest includes ff thin_slice_kernel=true for canary slice ids 42..47.

maria: @leo can you check kernel build agent status? might be compile timeouts during the deploy.

leo: agent pool shows spike in compile latency around 1761234000. some kernel builds failed and runtime fell back. Also batching metrics show microbatch thrash (rapid open/close).

ops-bot: Deploy event: deploy/2026-03-wave-7 started by @release-robot at 1761231200. Canary shift to 10% at 1761232600.

jamie: customer impact: a handful of high-throughput customers in EU saw increased tail latency and transient 429s due to short batching windows causing queue rejection. Not systemwide but visible in org-level SLO dashboards.

leo: immediate mitigations: 1) pause canary traffic (abort further ramp), 2) flip feature flag thin_slice_kernel=false for canary hosts, 3) revert to previous kernel variant on affected hosts or force recompile. Which order?

sarah: pause canary first. then flip ff. revert if instability persists.

jamie: executing pause-canary now -> `./deployctl traffic shift --deployment wave-7 --to 0% --scope canary`

ops-bot: Command acknowledged: traffic shift initiated by jamie at 1761234800. Target 0% canary.

leo: flipping FF for canary host group: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $KF" https://ff.internal/flags/thin_slice_kernel -d '{"enabled": false,"target":"canary"}'`

maria: flipped flag at 1761235120. telemetry shows kernel_selector fallbacks decreasing, batching windows slowly recovering.

jamie: customers still seeing occasional 5xx from queue rejects, but error rate trending down.

leo: recompile attempt for the preferred kernel started on a warm builder to avoid cold compile timeouts: `kite-build --kernel v3 --timeout 10m --priority high`

ops-bot: build job #7824 queued at 1761236000.

jamie: status update for exec: p95 dropped from 1.1s -> 420ms after pause+ff flip, throughput back to ~95% of baseline for canary traffic. Good but not fully recovered.

maria: I suggest we roll back the release for the remaining rollout wave to protect customers while we stabilize kernel builds. We can do a staggered rollback to avoid downstream thrash.

leo: agree. Plan: (A) stop rollout, (B) revert deployment on non-canary slices, (C) hold until kernel build pipeline fixed. Who coordinates rollback?

sarah: jamie can kick the rollback for the wave with `deployctl rollback --id deploy/2026-03-wave-7 --stagger 5m` and watch autoscaler. I'll coordinate with SRE for builders.

jamie: initiating rollback at 1761237000. `deployctl rollback --id deploy/2026-03-wave-7 --stagger 5m`

ops-bot: Rollback initiated by jamie at 1761237000. Estimated completion 1761240600.

leo: on the kernel side: builders saw a noisy neighbor causing compile spikes. SRE asked to isolate the pool and remove offending jobs. Maria, can you follow up with infra?

maria: already raised infra ticket INFRA-4571 and removed a heavy job. Builders look healthy now.

jamie: customer comms: alerted support channel to prepare a short note for impacted customers; flagged major accounts with ops contact.

sarah: paging/on-call: handing off to next oncall at 1761237800. @oncall-next you're up to monitor rollback progress, kernel build queue, and customer escalations. Key runbook: rollback_checklist.md -> confirm traffic shift to stable kernel and watch p95 < 300ms and error rate <0.1%.

oncall-next: acknowledged. I'll take it from here and post checkpoints every 15m.

leo: follow-up actions: 1) Improve kernel build backoff so we don't fallback prematurely. 2) Add a safety gate to prevent thin_slice_kernel enabling on global rollout unless build health is green. 3) Postmortem owner: jamie/sarah duo.

jamie: noted. setting postmortem owner tags and schedule.

ops-bot: Incident triage created: INC-2026-RT-278. Severity: Sev3 (customer-impacting tail latency).

maria: quick impact estimate for handoff: ~7 customers saw >50% tail latency spikes for 12–30 minutes, ~3 saw transient 429s. No billing-worthy data loss.

oncall-next: checkpoint at 1761239000: rollback 60% complete, p95 trending toward baseline (now ~280ms), builders stable. continuing to monitor.

jamie: thanks team. will capture timeline and config diffs for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
